#en: The manifest is little more than a smuggler's shopping list at first glance, tucked in with routine cargo notes and refuel records that span half the frontier, but the same corridors of mist and storms keep reappearing beside certain hull IDs and departure windows. Somewhere along the line, captains started timing their runs to manufactured weather, then telling dispatch it was just luck and good instincts. Seeing those entries laid out together turns rumor into a map; it proves someone has been selling quiet pathways through fog and cover, and that the same few outposts and stations keep sitting on the edges of those unnatural clouds. So far everything points back to a single hand on the pressure lines: a dead hunter's broken report, crops that grew through drought, and a corporate annex full of climate logs that never matched the sky.
zh:
这份舱单乍看不过是一张走私贩的购物清单，夹在横跨半个边境的例行货物备注与加油记录之间，但同样的雾气与风暴走廊一再出现在某些船体 ID 与离港时段旁边。
不知从哪一环起，船长们开始把航程安排得配合人造天气，然后告诉调度那只是运气加好直觉。
把这些条目摆在一起看，传言便变成一张地图；它证明有人一直在兜售穿过雾气与遮蔽的安静通路，也证明同样那几座哨站与空间站始终坐落在那几团不自然云层的边缘。
截至目前，一切都回指向操纵压力线的那一只手：一份死去的猎人的残缺报告、在干旱中仍抽穗生长的作物，以及一座气候日志与天空从不相符的企业附属区。

#en: The relay bunker is the clean choice, if there is such a thing. Concrete, rust, UC stonewalling; I know how that game plays. If those scan logs left any shadow behind, it will be in the gaps between what the grid admits and what actually crossed its airspace. Digging through half-dead consoles is slow work, but it might put a clear transponder on Rivet and names to the people who helped hide him.\n\nThe harvesting platform is something else. An old ore rig in an asteroid field is where you go when you want ghosts instead of answers. If there is a signal riding that telemetry, it is not just one man steering wrecks, it is a whole corridor being rewritten in the dark. That feels closer to whatever has been eating ships, but out there it will not just be rocks trying to kill me. Anyone who knows about that field is already lying by reflex.
zh:
中继碉堡是干净的选择——如果真有这种选择的话。混凝土、锈迹、联殖的推诿；我懂那套把戏。
如果那些扫描日志留下了任何影子，它就会藏在网格承认的东西与实际穿过其空域的东西之间的缝隙里。
在濒死的控制台里挖掘是慢工，但也许能给"铆钉"安上一枚清晰的应答器，并给那些帮他藏身的人安上名字。

采集平台则是另一回事。小行星带里一座旧矿石钻井，是你想要幽灵而非答案时会去的地方。
如果有信号骑在那道遥测上，那就不是一个人在操纵残骸，而是整条走廊正在黑暗中被重写。
那感觉更贴近一直在吞噬飞船的东西，但在那里，想杀我的不会只是岩石。任何知道那片场区的人，早就出于本能地在撒谎。

#en: That relay husk sits right where the map starts to lie, a kink nobody claims but everyone routes around. Cipher Blackfire on the ground means contracts, blind loyalty, and someone with enough money to hire professionals to stand on a corpse of a story. If I crack their filters, I see who approved every nudge, who signed off on turning traffic into targets. High risk, close-quarters, and the chance to put real names on all this drifting wreckage.  \n\nThe beacon is different. No guards, just distance and that thin, insistent song pushing ships sideways. If I tap it clean, I get a direction, not a dossier; I see where she is leaning the entire sky before the next correction locks in and becomes "standard practice." Quieter work, lonelier, but it might be the only way to follow her into whatever off-chart horizon she thinks belongs to her.
zh:
那具中继站空壳恰坐在地图开始说谎之处，一个无人认领、却人人绕行的扭结。
地面上有密码黑火帮，意味着合同、盲目忠诚，以及某个钱多到能雇专业人士站在一个故事的尸体上的人。
如果我破解他们的过滤器，我就能看到是谁批准了每一次推移、是谁签字同意把交通变成目标。高风险、近距离，以及给所有这些漂流的残骸安上真名的机会。

信标则不同。没有守卫，只有距离，以及那首细弱而固执、把飞船推向侧面的歌。
如果我把它干净地接入，我得到的是一个方向，而非一份档案；我能看到她在下一次修正锁定、变成"标准做法"之前，把整片天空倾向何方。更安静、更孤独的工作，但这也许是跟随她进入她认为属于自己的任何图外地平线的唯一办法。

#en: Neon's undergut is familiar rot. Bad lights, worse air, and enough Aurora in circulation that people forget what they signed or scrubbed. If I go back there, I am wading through rumor, half-truths, and clerks whose memories are for sale. The risk is getting buried under someone else's lie, but if those misfiled orders and half-finished recalls line up, they might finally sketch the outline of who started bending routes in the first place.\n\nDeimos is different. Scrapyard dust does not care what story you tell about a ship, the metal keeps its own. The Hellbound Dustwalkers are a problem, but at least their greed is honest; they will trade truth if the price is right. If that registry really has the unedited list of where those drives went after they were "scrapped," then it is the first clean spine I can run through all these quiet disasters.
zh:
霓虹城的下层内脏散发着熟悉的腐臭。糟糕的灯光、更糟的空气，以及流通得足够多的极光，让人忘记自己签过或擦去过什么。
如果我回到那里，我就要蹚过传言、半真半假，以及记忆待价而沽的文书。
风险是被别人的谎言埋葬，但如果那些归档错误的命令与半途而废的召回记录对上，它们也许终于能勾出究竟是谁最先开始弯折航线的轮廓。

火卫二则不同。废料场的尘土不在乎你怎么讲述一艘船的故事，金属只保留自己的说法。
地狱尘行者是个麻烦，但至少他们的贪婪很诚实；价钱合适，他们就肯交换真相。
如果那份名录真的存着那些引擎在被"拆解"之后去向的未删改清单，那它就是我能贯穿所有这些安静灾难的第一根干净的脊柱。

#en: The tower is the safer angle, at least on paper. Doors, corridors, hired guns that bleed like anyone else. If I peel back enough of those sealed records, I might finally see who paid for the first trial, who signed off when the numbers started looking wrong, and how a frontier backwater, a broken satellite, and a gutted courier all ended up on the same invisible ledger.\n\nThe beacon is pure Vector. No walls, no cover, just open sky and a sliver of metal humming between grav wells, its pulse bent into a code meant for her and no one else. If I crack that rhythm, I get her routes straight from the source, the timings she trusts with her own life. It is a narrower shot, higher risk, but it points past every proxy and middleman, toward the corridor she has been using to slip just beyond the reach of every faction still pretending they can control this.
zh:
塔是更安全的角度，至少纸面上如此。门、走廊、与任何人一样会流血的雇来的枪手。
如果我把那些封存记录揭开得足够多，也许终于能看到谁为第一次试验付了钱、在数字开始显得不对劲时是谁签了字，以及一座边境穷乡、一颗损坏的卫星和一艘被掏空的信使飞船，怎么会都落到同一本看不见的账册上。

信标则是纯粹的"向量"作风。没有墙、没有掩体，只有开阔的天空与一片在重力井之间嗡鸣的薄金属，它的脉冲被弯折成一段只给她、不给别人的密码。
如果我破解那段节奏，我就能直接从源头拿到她的航线，那些她以性命相托的时序。这是更窄的一枪、更高的风险，但它越过每一个代理与中间人，指向她一直用来滑到每个仍假装能控制这一切的势力触不可及之处的那条走廊。

#en: The barracks route is mud and ghosts. Old drill yards, Wayward Taskforce leaning on rifles and old habits, everyone pretending the scorch marks are just weathering. If there is a paper trail to the patterns, it is probably buried under redacted rosters and casualty drills no one logged aloud. Risk is close-quarters, people who know exactly how I think and move, but the payoff is hard proof: names, orders, something I can point to when the war stories start changing again.\n\nThe asteroid field is colder, cleaner in a way. Just rock, metal, and a listening device tuned to the echoes of every ship yanked a few degrees off-course. No veterans to stare holes through me, only whoever thinks this thing is worth ambushing over. The risk there is subtle: whatever I pull from those grav-wakes will not just confirm a pattern, it will show where all those lines converge next.
zh:
军营路线是泥泞与幽灵。旧操练场、靠步枪与旧习惯撑着的"任性特遣队"，所有人都假装那些焦痕只是风化。
如果这些图案真有一条纸面线索，它多半埋在涂黑的名册与无人出声记录过的伤亡演习之下。
风险是近距离，是那些对我的想法与行动方式了如指掌的人，但回报是硬证据：名字、命令，一些当战争故事再度改写时我能指认的东西。

小行星带更冷、某种程度上更干净。只有岩石、金属，以及一台调谐到每一艘被拽偏几度飞船回声的监听装置。
没有老兵用目光在我身上凿洞，只有那些认为这东西值得伏击的人。那里的风险是细微的：我从那些重力尾流中提取的一切，不仅会确认一个图案，还会显示所有那些线接下来汇聚到何处。

#en: The bunker planetside is slow, stale, and stubborn, like the concrete it is buried under. If I go back there, I am digging through old ghosts and older protocols, chasing anomalies that were never meant to see daylight again. The risk is more about who owned those records than what is guarding them now; step on the wrong file, and UC brass will notice someone is re-opening a story they worked hard to bury.\n\nHigh orbit is cleaner, colder, and sharper. The recon grid will not lie, not the way people do when paychecks and pensions are on the line. Out there, it is just vectors and timing, a map of where a certain rigger threaded the needle through restricted sky and which friendly transponders mysteriously went blind as he passed. The danger is physical instead of political; if anyone else is watching those buoys, they will not appreciate me reading over their shoulder.
zh:
行星地表的那座碉堡缓慢、陈腐而固执，就像它埋在底下所倚的混凝土。
如果我回到那里，我就要翻掘旧日的幽灵与更古老的协议，追查那些本不该重见天日的异常。
风险更多在于那些记录归谁所有，而非如今谁在看守它们；踩错文件，联殖高层就会注意到有人重新翻开了他们费尽力气掩埋的故事。

高轨道更干净、更冷、更锋利。侦察网格不会说谎，不会像人们在薪水和养老金悬于一线时那样说谎。
在那里，只有向量与时序，一张标出某名装配工在受限天空中如何穿针引线、以及哪些友方应答器在他经过时神秘失明的地图。
危险是物理性的而非政治性的；如果有别人也在看着那些浮标，他们可不会乐意我越肩偷看。

#en: That derelict plant down on the rock is the practical choice. Old Fleet math, stolen hardware, rust and dust between me and whatever she took from her own. If I dig it out, I get the before-and-after: where the routes used to run, and the exact moment she started bending them wrong. Less exposure, more time on the ground, more chance to walk out with something I can sell twice if I feel like getting clever.\n\nThat thin strip of orbit is the romantic choice, if you can call it that. No cover out there, just my hull, a twitchy sensor hub, and whoever has been watching the lanes like they belong to them. If I go, I am staring straight at the after: the pattern as it exists now, the invisible hand still pushing ships where they should not go. Higher risk, cleaner answers, and if I am right, I will be close enough to feel whoever built this second map breathing down my neck.
zh:
岩石上那座废弃工厂是务实的选择。旧舰队的算术、偷来的硬件，我与她从自己那里拿走的东西之间隔着锈与尘。
如果我把它挖出来，我就能得到前后对照：航线过去怎么走，以及她从哪一刻开始把它们弯错。
暴露更少、在地面待得更久、更有可能带着某件——如果我动了小聪明还能卖两次的东西——全身而退。

那一条狭薄的轨道是浪漫的选择，如果你能这么称呼它。那里没有掩体，只有我的船体、一座神经质的传感器枢纽，以及某个一直把航道当作自家产业来盯的人。
如果我去，我就是在直视"之后"：如今存在的图案，那只仍在把飞船推向不该去之处的看不见的手。更高风险、更干净的答案，如果我没判断错，我会近到能感到建造这第二张地图的人在我颈后呼气。

#en: The Freestar command trailer is mud, metal, and people who have seen too much go wrong without anyone listening. If I go back there and lean on that deputy, I might finally see whose names are written between his patrol notes, which routes were flagged before someone higher up ordered him to look away. That path smells like politics and buried reports, the kind of truth that gets you locked in a room with a non-disclosure and a smile.\n\nOut in far orbit, the relay and that tired hauler are just ghosts hanging over a quiet world. No briefings, no committees, just raw signal where someone has been carving new lines into the sky. If I chase that lead, I put myself between whoever is buying these lies and the man selling them, with nothing between us but cold vacuum and whatever defenses he thinks are enough. One path walks into offices; the other walks straight into his shadow.
zh:
星联指挥拖车是泥泞、金属，以及一些眼睁睁看着太多事情出错却无人倾听的人。
如果我回到那里去逼那位副手，也许终于能看到他的巡逻笔记之间写着谁的名字、哪些航线在上级命令他别过头去之前就被标记过。
这条路闻起来像政治与被掩埋的报告——那种会让你被关进一间屋子、递上一份保密协议和一个微笑的真相。

在遥远轨道上，那座中继站和那艘疲惫的运货船只是悬在一颗安静世界上方的幽灵。没有简报、没有委员会，只有某人一直在天空中刻下新线的原始信号。
如果我追那条线索，我就把自己置于买这些谎言的人与卖这些谎言的人之间，我们之间只有冰冷的真空，以及他认为足够的防御。一条路走进办公室；另一条径直走进他的影子。

#en: New Atlantis means walking into the beating heart of traffic control and pretending I am just another hauler with time to kill. Manifests, docking logs, customs scans, the whispered side deals in freight offices where clerks know exactly which shortcuts exist and pretend they do not. If there is a paper trail to her corridors, it will be under bright lights and uniformed indifference, buried in arguments over fuel surcharges and who owes who a favor. Safe, on the surface. Loud. Crowded. Easy to disappear in, or be disappeared from.\n\nThe relay in deep orbit is the opposite; no witnesses but whatever sits on that junk hauler's guns and whatever traps she left wired into the beacon's shell. Out there I would be reading her work directly, stripped of official excuses, watching the numbers curve toward whatever she is circling. Quieter, riskier, closer to the bones of the pattern.
zh:
新亚特兰蒂斯城意味着走进交通管制跳动的心脏，假装我只是又一个闲得发慌的运货船司机。
舱单、停靠日志、海关扫描，以及货运办公室里低声的私下交易——那里的文书清楚知道有哪些捷径，却假装不知道。
如果她的走廊有一条纸面线索，它就会暴露在明亮的灯光与穿制服的冷漠之下，埋在关于燃油附加费与谁欠谁人情的争吵里。表面上安全。嘈杂。拥挤。容易消失其中，或被从中消失。

深轨中的中继站恰恰相反；除了那艘废料运货船上的火炮、以及她接进信标外壳里的陷阱，没有别的目击者。
在那里，我将直接阅读她的作品，剥去官方的借口，看着数字弯向她所环绕的东西。更安静、更冒险，也更贴近图案的骨架。

#en: Gagarin Landing is the quiet kind of crooked, the kind that lives in ink and routine. If Vector has friends, they will be the clerks who learned which hulls to wave through and which anomalies to file as "resolved" without looking up. Digging there means talking to people who survive by not remembering too much and prying at patterns buried under years of freight and favors. Safer on paper, maybe, but it puts me in the same room as anyone who profited from looking the other way.\n\nThe recon grid in orbit is a different problem. No bribes, no shrugs, just hard numbers and a lot of cold space between me and whoever does not want those numbers read. If his signature is split across those sensors, it will tell me exactly how he is carving his own lanes and where they bend away from the public corridors. High risk, and if a navy handler notices me snooping, I become the anomaly to erase.
zh:
加加林着陆点是那种安静的歪斜，活在墨水与例行公事里的歪斜。
如果"向量"有朋友，那就是那些学会了哪些船体该放行、哪些异常该在不抬头的状态下归档为"已解决"的文书。
在那里挖掘，就意味着与那些靠不多记、并撬开埋在多年货运与人情之下的图案过活的人交谈。纸面上也许更安全，但它会把我放进与任何靠别过头去获利的人同一个房间。

轨道上的侦察网格是另一个问题。没有贿赂、没有耸肩，只有硬数字，以及我与那些不想让这些数字被读到的人之间大片冰冷太空。
如果他的特征分散在那些传感器上，它就会准确告诉我他如何刻出自己的航道，以及它们在何处背离公共走廊。高风险，而如果某位海军管事注意到我在窥探，我就成了那个需要被抹除的异常。

#en: If I stay in the tunnels, I am chasing voices and paper. The Well stinks of recycled air and rumor, but buried under the gossip and changed stories there is a hard record of what she pushed where and when. Going back into those cramped offices and kiosk backrooms means dealing with people who owe her, fear her, or both but if I want to know who vanished into her promises, their names are written down there somewhere, however deep she tried to bury them.  \n\nIf I go up instead, into that quiet ring of forgotten hardware above the planet, I am chasing the way she bent the sky. No crowds, just old firmware and course corrections that never quite matched their declared targets. If she hid the true map anywhere, it will be in those half ignored survey returns, the ones that kept nudging traffic toward the same blank patch of nothing every time some desperate settler bought hope off the record.
zh:
如果我留在隧道里，我追的就是声音与纸面。深井区散发着循环空气与传言的臭气，但在闲话与被改口的故事之下，埋着一份关于她在何时把什么推向何处的硬记录。
回到那些逼仄的办公室与售货亭后室，就意味着与欠她人情、怕她、或两者兼具的人打交道，但如果我想知道是谁消失进了她的承诺里，他们的名字就写在那里某处，无论她把它埋得多深。

如果我转而向上，进入行星上方那圈被遗忘硬件的安静环带，我追的就是她弯折天空的方式。
没有人群，只有旧固件与那些从未真正匹配申报目标的航向修正。
如果她把真正的地图藏在某处，那就在那些被半忽视的勘测回传里——每当有绝望的定居者私下买下希望，它们就把交通轻推向同一片空白的虚无。
